Type.evidence_source: One purpose of the study outlined in this paper was to gain further insight into the factors that may buffer L/B/G youth from suicidality.

Area.evidence_source: While considerable research has highlighted the factors that increase L/B/G youth suicide risk, there has been much less emphasis on protective factors (Anderson, 1998; Conceptual Foundations Workgroup, 1995). Resiliency factors encapsulate ". . . layers of protective and adaptive mechanisms–meaning specific traits, conditions, and situations-to circumvent health–damaging behaviors and alter or reverse predictions of negative outcome" (Clark, Marsh, Davis, Igoe, & Stember, 1996, p. 1). To some extent, studies of risk factors have served to illustrate possible protective factors by default. For instance, whereas young men who suffer chronic social rejection and isolation may be particularly prone to suicidal thoughts and behaviour, the antithesis (i.e., social integration, positive acceptance, and strong social support) may help protect against L/B/G suicide attempts (Hershberger et al., 1997; Rotheram-Borus & Fernandez, 1995). Other resiliency factors may include increased community-level support, early accurate education about homosexuality, and the availability of positive L/B/G role models (Olson & King, 1995). Essentially, all of these factors may help to establish, support, and promote high self-esteem, a powerful resiliency factor for L/B/G suicide (Remafedi et al., 1991; Remafedi et al., 1998; Rotheram-Borus & Fernandez, 1995; Saunders & Valente, 1987).
